reason: Already litigated and explicitly ruled out, and the fix is worse than the line it replaces. (1) SETTLED. This exact move - turn the morning's note into a count - was proposed in round 2 and refused by name in the verdict for wedding-morning-is-written-as-admin: 'DO NOT switch the day-of note to a count... received surfaces name things and never tally, and "8 things got you here" would reinstate the tracker voice on the most received screen in the set.' The current string is not filler, it is round 1's own remediation for the-day-reads-as-a-closed-ticket, whose refuter specified the register in writing: 'one present-tense sentence that neither counts nor congratulates.' Round 4's verdict for morning-addresses-the-wrong-reader records it as 'round 1's remediation, kept by round 2's measuring verdict and refuted again in round 3... reversing any of them trades a fixed defect for an old one.' Four rounds have attacked this line and none has landed. (2) THE SAME SEAT PRAISED IT TWICE. round-3/seat-taste calls it 'a designed decision with feeling in it, and it is the reason this is a 7.3 and not a 6'; round-7/seat-taste calls it 'the one sentence in the artifact that is written rather than specified.' Round 8 calls the identical string flat. That oscillation with no new evidence is taste asserted as a defect. (3) THE FIX BREAKS THE COMPOSITION'S ONE IDEA. Driven at state=day, 390 and 1440, with the proposed string patched into .b-dayNote: the block reads 'Today' at 96px, the date, the indigo rule, then '274 days since we said yes.' at 15px / fore-62. The whole designed move of this screen - and of the gate assertions 'the arrived count is a word' and 'the arrived count keeps the count's register' - is that on the day the instrument stops counting and the count becomes a word. The fix puts a numeral back into that block, four lines under the slot it was retired from, and puts it in the body whisper register while lock.md reserves 96 and 148 for 'the count, which is the whole composition.' Two magnitudes, one block; it reads as a receipt under a headline, not as a sentence. (4) IT DEPENDS ON ONE LUCKY FIXTURE STRING. The line only sings because this fixture's first covered moment happens to be 'We said yes'. Running the proposed expression over the real title set the same code produces '168 days since the orchard reserved.', '63 days since menu tasting at the orchard.', '56 days since send the invitations.' - bathos, ungrammatical, and the blanket .toLowerCase() destroys the proper noun. The file already knows better: behindBlock lowercases only the leading character (dropped[0].title.charAt(0).toLowerCase() + slice(1)) for exactly this reason. The proposed fallback guards only the empty plan, not the ordinary one. (5) IT DUPLICATES A FACT ALREADY ON THE SCREEN. '274' and 'We said yes' are printed verbatim on the same column 550px down the back rail. (6) MINOR FACTUAL SLIP. It is the eighth row on the rail, not the ninth; the ninth 'moment' is the undated cancelled hotel shortlist, which renders outside the measure. (7) 'Buried behind a disclosure' argues against a named, published decision of this room - the approach is ink / measured / folded / once - and the morning does draw the instrument: the gate already proves 'the morning draws the past as the instrument' at two pixels a day, which is round 4's answer to this same complaint. Neither gate assertion the brief names would fail on the fix; that is not the reason it is refuted. It is refuted because it reverses a four-round-old ratified decision, degrades on any plan but this one, and puts the count back on the one morning the design exists to take it away.
sharpenedFix: Take nothing here. If a future round still wants the distance stated on the morning, the only version worth building is one that does not tally and does not depend on a fixture title: open .b-behindDetails by default on state=day so the 274-day rail - the instrument already drawn, already gate-proven - is the thing that states the distance in its own language, and leave .b-dayNote alone. That is a composition decision with a real cost (round 4 already refuted day-disclosure-opens-past-the-fold), not a copy swap, and it is not this finding.
